proof:
Source: Step 3 of the parent proof, which replaces Simon Ch. 6, Remark 2.35. It rests on the representation formula of D. Gilbarg and N. S. Trudinger, Elliptic Partial Differential Equations of Second Order, Lemma 7.14, and the elementary potential estimate of their §7.8. Throughout, n = m + 1 ≥ 1, |·| is the Euclidean norm on ℝⁿ, Lⁿ = volume, and B_ρ(y) is the open ball. We write |w|^{1−n} for (|w|^{n−1})^{−1}; in Lean this is (‖w‖^m)⁻¹, because the natural-number exponent 1 − n would truncate.

1. Constants and polar coordinates. Let ω_n := Lⁿ(B_1(0)) ∈ (0, ∞) and C := ((n+1)/n)·ω_n^{−1/n}; C depends only on m. Let σ := volume.toSphere be the surface measure on the unit sphere S^{n−1}. By Measure.toSphere_apply_univ, σ(S^{n−1}) = n·ω_n.
 Polar coordinates (P): for every g ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ),
  ∫_{ℝⁿ} g(t) dt = ∫_{S^{n−1}} ∫_0^∞ r^{n−1} g(rθ) dr dσ(θ).
 This follows from Measure.measurePreserving_homeomorphUnitSphereProd, which carries Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ∖{0} to σ ⊗ r^{n−1}dr on S^{n−1} × (0, ∞), together with the fact that {0} is Lⁿ-null. The Lean ingredients are:
  – integral_subtype_comap with restrict_compl_singleton;
  – MeasurePreserving.integral_comp and MeasurePreserving.integrable_comp_emb, for the measurable embedding of the homeomorphism;
  – integrableOn_iff_comap_subtypeVal;
  – integral_prod (Fubini);
  – integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul, to unfold the radial measure Measure.volumeIoiPow (n−1).
 Mathlib's proof of integral_fun_norm_addHaar is the template.
 For radial functions, integral_fun_norm_addHaar gives ∫ h(|w|) dw = n ω_n ∫_0^∞ r^{n−1} h(r) dr, and integrableOn_fun_norm_addHaar gives the matching integrability criterion. Hence, for every ρ > 0, w ↦ |w|^{1−n} is integrable on B_ρ(0), because its radial profile r^{n−1}·r^{1−n} = 1 is integrable on (0, ρ), and
  (R) ∫_{B_ρ(0)} |w|^{1−n} dw = n ω_n ∫_0^ρ 1 dr = n ω_n ρ.
 These formulas hold uniformly for every n ≥ 1, so no case distinction is needed; for n = 1, S⁰ = {±1} and n ω_n = 2.

2. The kernels. For j ∈ Fin n let K_j(w) := w_j/(n ω_n |w|ⁿ) for w ≠ 0 and K_j(0) := 0 (in Lean, division by 0 already gives 0). K_j is Borel measurable, and |K_j(w)| ≤ |w|^{1−n}/(n ω_n) because |w_j| ≤ |w|. By Step 1, |·|^{1−n} is integrable on every ball, so K_j is integrable on every ball by domination. Hence K_j is locally integrable.

3. Definition and smoothness of ψ_j. Fix a ∈ C_c^∞(ℝⁿ) and M with |a| ≤ M everywhere. Put ψ_j := K_j ⋆ a, the convolution with the scalar multiplication pairing (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ): ψ_j(y) = ∫ K_j(t) a(y − t) dt (convolution_def). K_j is locally integrable and a is C^∞ with compact support, so ψ_j is C^∞ by HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_right. Its derivative at y is (K_j ⋆ Da)(y) for the precomposed pairing (HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right). Evaluating at e_k with convolution_precompR_apply gives, for every k,
  ∂_kψ_j(y) = ∫ K_j(t) ∂_k a(y − t) dt.

4. Representation formula: Σ_j ∂_jψ_j(y) = a(y) for every y ∈ ℝⁿ. Fix y.
 (a) Ray FTC. Let θ be a unit vector and h(r) := a(y − rθ). Then h is C¹ with h′(r) = −Da(y − rθ)θ, and h(r) = 0 for all large r because a has compact support. By integral_Ioi_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto,
  ∫_0^∞ Da(y − rθ)θ dr = h(0) − lim_{r→∞} h(r) = a(y).
 (b) Pointwise identity. Expanding t in the standard basis gives Da(y − t)t = Σ_j t_j ∂_j a(y − t). Hence, for t ≠ 0,
  Σ_j K_j(t) ∂_j a(y − t) = G(t) := Da(y − t)t/(n ω_n |t|ⁿ),
 and both sides are 0 at t = 0.
 (c) Integrability. Each t ↦ K_j(t) ∂_j a(y − t) is integrable, because K_j is locally integrable and ∂_j a is continuous with compact support (HasCompactSupport.convolutionExists_right). Therefore G is integrable and, by Step 3 with k = j, Σ_j ∂_jψ_j(y) = Σ_j ∫ K_j(t) ∂_j a(y − t) dt = ∫ G(t) dt.
 (d) Apply (P) to G. For r > 0 and |θ| = 1,
  r^{n−1} G(rθ) = r^{n−1}·Da(y − rθ)(rθ)/(n ω_n rⁿ) = Da(y − rθ)θ/(n ω_n).
 By (a) the inner radial integral is a(y)/(n ω_n). Integrating this constant over S^{n−1} gives σ(S^{n−1})·a(y)/(n ω_n) = a(y). Hence Σ_j ∂_jψ_j(y) = a(y).

5. The sup bound. Let S := tsupport a. It is compact, so Lⁿ(S) < ∞. Also M ≥ |a(0)| ≥ 0.
 Case Lⁿ(S) = 0. The open set {a ≠ 0} is contained in S, so it is Lⁿ-null. A nonempty open subset of ℝⁿ has positive Lebesgue measure, so this set is empty. Hence a ≡ 0 and ψ_j ≡ 0, and |ψ_j(y)| = 0 ≤ C·M·0^{1/n} = 0 (the exponent 1/n is positive).
 Case Lⁿ(S) > 0. Put ρ := (Lⁿ(S)/ω_n)^{1/n} > 0, so that Lⁿ(S) = ω_n ρⁿ. Fix y and let S_y := {t : y − t ∈ S}. The map t ↦ y − t preserves Lebesgue measure, so Lⁿ(S_y) = Lⁿ(S). Since a(y − t) = 0 for t ∉ S_y and |a| ≤ M, Step 2 gives
  |ψ_j(y)| ≤ ∫_{S_y} |K_j(t)|·|a(y − t)| dt ≤ (M/(n ω_n)) ∫_{S_y} |t|^{1−n} dt.
 Split S_y into S_y ∩ B_ρ(0) and S_y ∖ B_ρ(0).
 – By (R), ∫_{S_y ∩ B_ρ(0)} |t|^{1−n} dt ≤ n ω_n ρ.
 – On S_y ∖ B_ρ(0) we have |t| ≥ ρ, so |t|^{1−n} ≤ ρ^{1−n}. That part of the integral is therefore at most ρ^{1−n} Lⁿ(S_y) = ρ^{1−n} ω_n ρⁿ = ω_n ρ.
 Hence ∫_{S_y} |t|^{1−n} dt ≤ (n + 1) ω_n ρ, and
  |ψ_j(y)| ≤ (M/(n ω_n))·(n + 1) ω_n ρ = ((n+1)/n)·M·ω_n^{−1/n}·Lⁿ(S)^{1/n} = C·M·Lⁿ(S)^{1/n}.

6. Conclusion. The functions ψ_j of Step 3 are C^∞. They satisfy Σ_j ∂_jψ_j = a (Step 4) and |ψ_j(y)| ≤ C·M·Lⁿ(tsupport a)^{1/n} for all j and y (Step 5), with C from Step 1 independent of a and M. In the Lean statement, Lⁿ(tsupport a) is finite and equals (volume (tsupport a)).toReal, the exponent 1/((m:ℝ)+1) equals 1/n, and ∂_jψ_j(y) is fderiv ℝ (ψ j) y (EuclideanSpace.single j 1). ∎
key_steps: Fix ω_n = Lⁿ(B_1) and C = ((n+1)/n)ω_n^{−1/n}. Use polar coordinates, where σ(S^{n−1}) = nω_n, and the radial integral ∫_{B_ρ}|w|^{1−n} = nω_nρ.
The kernels K_j(w) = w_j/(nω_n|w|ⁿ) are locally integrable, with |K_j(w)| ≤ |w|^{1−n}/(nω_n).
ψ_j := K_j ⋆ a is C^∞, and ∂_kψ_j = K_j ⋆ ∂_k a (convolution with a compactly supported smooth function).
Representation Σ_j ∂_jψ_j(y) = ∫ Da(y−t)t/(nω_n|t|ⁿ) dt = a(y), from polar coordinates centred at 0 and the FTC along the rays r ↦ y − rθ (Gilbarg–Trudinger, Lemma 7.14).
Sup bound: split y − spt a (same measure as spt a) at the radius ρ = (Lⁿ(spt a)/ω_n)^{1/n} to get |ψ_j| ≤ ((n+1)/n)Mρ = C·M·Lⁿ(spt a)^{1/n}. The case Lⁿ(spt a) = 0 forces a ≡ 0.
